title: Sound & microphone
blurb: No sound, wrong speaker, crackling, microphone not picking up.

remedies.title: Volume is too low even at 100%
remedies.why: An app's own volume, a quiet video, or the speaker's limits; Windows also has loudness tools.

steps.text: Turn up the app's and the video's own volume, and check the mixer.
Turn on Loudness Equalization: Sound control panel › speakers › Properties › Enhancements (if offered).
Check the Mac's Balance is centred and the output volume is up in Sound settings.
For laptops, external speakers or headphones are much louder.

remedies.title: Sound only comes out of one side
remedies.why: Balance is off-centre, Mono audio is on, or the plug/cable is damaged.

steps.text: Check Mono audio is off: Accessibility › Audio.
Check the balance: Sound control panel › device › Properties › Levels › Balance.
Centre the Balance in Sound settings and turn off Mono in Accessibility › Audio.
Try other headphones; one-sided sound on one pair means a broken wire.

remedies.title: Turn off (or on) notification and system sounds
remedies.why: System and app sounds are set separately from music and calls.

steps.text: Settings › System › Notifications: turn off sounds per app; Sound control panel › Sounds tab › Sound scheme: No Sounds.
Sound › Sound Effects for alert sounds; Notifications for per-app sounds.

remedies.title: USB headset, speakers or microphone not detected
remedies.why: Not enough power through a hub, a missing driver, or the device needs its own app.

steps.text: Plug straight into the computer and try another port.
Look under Audio inputs and outputs in Device Manager for warnings.
Check it shows in Audio MIDI Setup.
Install the maker's driver for audio interfaces.

remedies.title: People hear background noise, typing or a hum
remedies.why: The microphone picks up the room; laptop mics sit right next to the keyboard and fan.

steps.text: Turn on noise suppression in the meeting app (Teams: Noise suppression High; Zoom: Background noise).
Use a headset microphone close to your mouth.
A hum on a wired mic often comes from a charger; unplug it to test.
Turn on Voice Clarity / Voice Isolation if the system offers it (Mac: Control Center › Mic Mode during a call).
